product_identity.short_description: AI-agnostic vendor intelligence platform that aggregates products and services from multiple vendors into a single curated catalog with selective discovery, user-owned data, and flexible AI integration.
product_identity.core_value_proposition: One curated catalog assembled from many vendor sources — website, PDF, manual, and future connectors — with AI enrichment that is provider-agnostic and always validated before import.
product_identity.long_description: Source BlendR lets businesses pull products and services from multiple vendors into a single owned catalog. It emphasizes discovery before import, keeps catalog items as the primary entity, treats manual entry as a first-class workflow, runs all scraping and AI work in background workers, and keeps AI providers swappable via an adapter architecture. The platform is intentionally modular and extensible to support future connectors, vendors, and AI providers without redesign.

strategic_intent.primary_objective: Be the single owned catalog that businesses use to unify vendor product and service data across many sources, with AI assistance that never locks them to a single provider.
secondary_objectives: Eliminate manual copy/paste vendor aggregation by automating discovery and normalization
Make AI an implementation detail that can be swapped without business-logic changes
Give users control over what enters their catalog via discovery sessions and user review
Enable downstream business outputs (flyers, quotes, collections, analytics) from one owned catalog
strategic_intent.business_model_hint: B2B subscription SaaS with multi-tenant workspaces; potential per-seat or per-workspace pricing; future team and marketplace features
strategic_intent.competitive_positioning: Vendor-agnostic and AI-provider-agnostic catalog platform; not an AI platform, not a marketplace, not a POS, not an ERP

problem_framing.core_problem: Businesses maintain product and service data across many vendors using manual, fragmented, and inconsistent processes. Catalogs drift, copy/paste errors propagate, and there is no single owned source of truth that works with any AI provider.
problems_addressed: Vendor product data is scattered across websites, PDFs, and manual knowledge
Manual copy/paste import is slow, error-prone, and not scalable
Existing tools lock users to a single vendor or a single AI provider
No safe staging area exists between discovery and catalog import
Pricing, margin, and catalog structure differ across vendors with no normalization
Business outputs (flyers, quotes, collections) must be rebuilt from scratch each time
problem_framing.primary_outcome: A single curated, user-owned catalog enriched by swappable AI from many vendor sources, with deterministic validation and user review before anything enters inventory.

business_direction.primary_revenue_hint: B2B SaaS subscription per workspace; future team seats, advanced AI usage, and marketplace integrations
business_direction.target_market_hint: Promotional products, distributors, retailers, service aggregators, and businesses that resell or repackage multiple vendors' offerings
business_direction.launch_focus: Single-tenant workspaces with core import-to-catalog workflows; multi-tenant foundation; future team support

differentiation_hypotheses.hypothesis: AI-provider agnosticism is a meaningful differentiator because users distrust being locked to a single AI vendor for business-critical catalog operations.
Discovery Sessions (staging before import) reduce data quality risk and are not common in competitor tools.
Universal Catalog Items (products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, installation) under one entity are a differentiator because most competitors are product-only.
Document Memory and Vendor Memory (versioned change tracking across imports) create switching costs and retention.

known_constraints: AI is optional; a user must be able to run the platform without configuring any AI provider
No automatic imports — Discovery Sessions always gate catalog entry
Manual entry must remain a first-class workflow alongside automated import
PDF imports are equal in status to website imports
Background workers must handle scraping and AI processing so the UI stays responsive
Playwright is the locked web discovery engine
Catalog Items replace any Product-only architecture

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Build Source BlendR as an AI-agnostic Vendor Intelligence Platform: multi-tenant workspaces, Playwright-first website discovery, PDF catalog extraction, Discovery Session staging before import, Universal Catalog Items (products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, installation), AI Provider Adapter Architecture with capability routing, background workers, and deferred future features per the PRD.
alternatives_considered: Single AI provider only (rejected: violates AI-agnostic locked principle)
Auto-import without Discovery Sessions (rejected: violates discovery-before-import locked principle)
Product-only catalog (rejected: violates Universal Catalog Items locked decision)
Plug-in marketplace architecture (rejected: explicitly out of scope in Inference Layer summary)
key_decisions: Playwright is the locked web discovery engine
AI is provider-agnostic via adapter architecture and capability router
Discovery Sessions always gate catalog imports
Universal Catalog Items replace Product-only schema
Manual entry is a first-class workflow; platform runs with zero AI providers
Background workers handle scraping and AI processing
PDF imports are equal in status to website imports
Flyer and Quote Builders are should-have; may be trimmed or deferred to protect MVP risk

assumptions.assumption: Playwright + AI-assisted site analysis handles the majority of target-market vendor sites.
Target users value provider independence and owned catalog data.
Discovery Sessions are accepted as friction-positive vs auto-import competitors.
Universal Catalog Items cover the target market without forcing partial re-architecture.
Background workers keep the UI responsive for expected scrape/AI durations without a streaming UI.

risks.description: Playwright reliability across diverse vendor sites
Target market too small or unwilling to pay

downstream_impact: Stage 2 must validate differentiation hypotheses, market demand, and technical assumptions (Playwright reliability, OCR/AI extraction quality, Universal Catalog schema coverage).
Stage 3 must lock adapter interface, capability router contract, validation engine contract, multi-tenancy isolation boundary, and queue/timeout strategy.
Stage 4 must validate Discovery Session UX and catalog browsing UX.
Stage 5 slices import-to-catalog flow, adapter architecture, and catalog as launch-critical; flyer/quote as should-have.
Stage 6 acceptance criteria must include AI extraction-quality tests per capability and validation engine tests.
